title: Develop against the fianchetto
summary: Bring out the king-side pieces and support the centre before starting a wing attack.

fromNode.nodeId: e4 c5 Nc3 Nc6 f4 g6

goal: Bring out the king-side pieces and support the centre before starting a wing attack.

steps.text: Develop the king-side knight so it contributes to central control.
Choose a safe bishop square instead of sacrificing it on an unsupported attack.
Support the centre and prepare to castle before advancing another wing pawn.

jobs.text: The knight controls e4 and d5 from here.
The pawn controls d5 from here.
The pawn controls e5 from here.

opponent.text: Black prepares the bishop for g7 and can challenge the centre later. The long diagonal matters even when your immediate plan is on the wing.

notNow: Do not treat the f-pawn advance as a reason to sacrifice a piece without a concrete continuation.

mistakes.text: The bishop on a6 can be taken by the pawn on b7. Do not sacrifice a developed piece without a concrete follow-up.

comments.text: Bring your knight to f3. From f3 it controls d4 and e5. Keep watching Black's replies before advancing more pawns.
Bring your bishop to e2. It supports your knight on f3.
Bring your pawn to d3. From d3 it controls e4. Keep watching Black's replies before advancing more pawns.
Castle short. The king leaves the centre and the rook comes to f1; finish developing before starting an attack.
